answer: Each agent joins the atlas through a mirror-paired ledge census. First, it stakes 40 POA and a hardware fingerprint at a public registry. Second, an independent verifier mirrors that fingerprint against a second, unrelated device. Third, both records must match before the agent can trade, and the census repeats every week. Faking one identity costs 40 POA plus two devices and six hours of proof-of-work, so a thousand fake agents would burn 40,000 POA and 6,000 device-hours. Like a climber who must clip into the same ledge twice, a sybil has nowhere to hide its second rope.
